title: Product PRD: Unified Inference v17 — Overview, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document captures the product requirements, high-level design, roadmap themes, pricing/packaging updates, and release notes for Unified Inference v17 (codename: Orion). v17 continues Redwood's focus on production economics: lower unit cost, tighter latency SLOs for tail latency, and new rollout controls for multi-variant model routing.

Background and goals:
- Problem statement: Customers building inference-backed features need predictable latency and lower per-token cost while supporting multiple model variants and deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Primary goals for v17:
  1. Reduce average per-token cost by 10-20% for common web workloads via improved batching and caching heuristics.
  2. Reduce p95 token latency by 15% for 2k+ sequence workloads on Dedicated and Hosted tiers.
  3. Launch model-variant routing policies (cost-aware, latency-aware, and fallback) with A/B and canary rollout primitives in the Console and API.
  4. Simplify pricing & packaging: introduce a tiered Dedicated SKU and optional Quality SLA add-on.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope:
  - Serving runtime heuristics: dynamic batching, KV prefetch improvements, and prefix cache eviction policies.
  - API surface: new route-config fields for routing_policy and rollout_strategy.
  - Console: rollout UI, cost insights per-route, and model variant analytics.
  - Pricing: new Dedicated Standard/Pro SKUs and a Quality SLA add-on.
- Out of scope:
  - New model architecture support (e.g., new attention types beyond existing kernel set).
  - On-prem packaging changes to install process (constituent work tracked separately in eng-private-deployments).

Requirements (product & functional):
- MUST: API accepts route configuration with fields: routing_policy (cost|latency|balanced), primary_model_id, fallback_model_ids (ordered), rollout_strategy (canary|ab|immediate), rollout_percent (0-100).
- MUST: Console exposes a Rollouts page that shows per-variant latency, cost-per-1k-tokens, error-rate, and traffic percent in real time (refresh <= 5s for active canaries).
- MUST: Hosting runtime will provide per-request metadata (model_id, quantization_profile, node_type) to tracing and billing pipelines.
- MUST: Dedicated Standard and Pro SKUs with clear throughput units (RTU) definitions and paging for burst capacity.
- SHOULD: Autoscaling policies respect rollout_policy so that canaries do not trigger overprovisioning of Pro capacity.
- SHOULD: Provide an SDK helper that wraps route config creation and exposes a safe default policy: balanced routing with automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant on capacity pressure.

Non-functional requirements (SLO & metrics):
- Latency SLOs (internal targets): p50 <= 60ms token, p95 <= 220ms token for typical web workloads (<= 2k tokens) on Dedicated Pro / Hosted premium.
- Cost target: 10-20% reduction in per-token cost (measured across key customers' web-qa workloads) within 90 days after rollout.
- Reliability: rollout failure rate (failed canary switches requiring manual rollback) < 1% per rollout.
- Observability: every route must emit the following tags: route_id, customer_id, model_id, variant_id, routing_policy.

High-level design overview:
- Components involved:
  - Runtime Optimizer: selects batching window and kernel sequences per request. New heuristic: adaptive_window that expands for bursty short-request patterns and contracts for long-sequence requests.
  - Routing Service: policy engine evaluating routing_policy and live telemetry (latency, cost_estimate, regional_availability).
  - Rollout Manager: orchestrates traffic shifts, supports timed automatic rollbacks, and exposes canary dashboards.
  - Billing & Cost Insights pipeline: aggregates per-token cost estimates and attributes to route/model.

Design details (key decisions):
- Routing policy semantics:
  - cost: prefers variants with lower estimated per-token cost; secondary tie-breaker is latency.
  - latency: favors lowest estimated expected tail latency; secondary tie-breaker is cost.
  - balanced: heuristic that optimizes a weighted objective (0.6 latency, 0.4 cost) and aims to meet both budgets.
- Fallback semantics:
  - Fallbacks are ordinal: system will attempt fallback_model_ids in order. Each fallback attempt increments a failure counter and records the reason (capacity|error|latency-exceeded).
- Rollout strategies:
  1) Canary: increment traffic from rollout_percent start (typically 1%) to target over a configurable window (defaults: 10% over 24h).
  2) A/B: stable split with statistical monitoring; experiment results recorded to releases-experiments dataset.
  3) Immediate: immediate flip to new variant (for emergency fixes).

API examples (request JSON snippets):
- Route create (example):
{
  "route_name": "qa-chat",
  "primary_model_id": "open-redwood-3b",
  "fallback_model_ids": ["open-redwood-1b-quant", "open-llama-3b"],
  "routing_policy": "balanced",
  "rollout_strategy": "canary",
  "rollout_percent": 5
}

Console UX notes:
- New Rollouts page under Routes shows a table and per-route detail pane with graphs for latency, cost-per-1k, errors, and a timeline of rollout events.
- Inline quick actions: pause rollout, rollback, increase percent, open support case.

Roadmap and themes (next 6 months):
- Q3 2027 (now): v17 GA for Hosted and Dedicated Standard; Console rollout controls beta.
- Q4 2027: Dedicated Pro launch, Quality SLA add-on, extended observability retention for rollout analytics (90 days).
- Q1 2028: Private deployment support for routing_policy and rollout manager (VPC-only control plane).
- Cross-cutting: continuous perf tuning and kernel selection improvements for long-sequence models.

Pricing & packaging changes (customer-facing summary):
- Hosted: no change to per-token baseline pricing. New per-route cost-insight dashboards available to all Hosted customers.
- Dedicated: introduce two SKUs:
  - Dedicated Standard: baseline reserved RTUs with soft burst; ideal for startups and mid-market (monthly commitment).
  - Dedicated Pro: guaranteed RTUs, lower per-token price, priority SLAs (99.95% uptime) and lower p95 latency targets.
- Quality SLA add-on: optional 12-month commitment that backs per-route latency guarantees (credits for missed SLOs) and extended tracing retention (90 days).
- Pricing examples table:
| SKU | Monthly commit | Typical p95 token latency (<=2k) | Effective per-token price (estimate) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Dedicated Standard | $12k | 350ms | $0.00060 |
| Dedicated Pro | $60k | 220ms | $0.00038 |

Release notes (v17.0.0 — 2027-09-01):
- Features:
  - Launch: routing_policy and rollout_strategy fields in Routes API and Console rollout manager (GA for Hosted; beta for Dedicated Pro).
  - New adaptive batching heuristic (adaptive_window) reducing average cost by ~12% in internal benchmarks.
  - Console: Rollouts page and per-route cost insights (refresh <=5s for active canaries).
- Fixes and improvements:
  - Reduced p95 token latency by 16% on typical web workloads (internal synthetic test).
  - Billing pipeline now records model_variant metadata for more granular cost attribution.
  - Improved fallback logging to include failure reason and capacity snapshot.
- Known issues:
  - Private deployments: Rollout Manager UI not yet available in air-gapped installs (work planned for Q1 2028).
  - Edge case: extremely bursty short-request patterns can temporarily increase tail latency under cost routing policy; mitigation: conservative rollout defaults.

Rollout and launch plan:
1) Week 0 (2027-09-01): GA announcement for Hosted; feature flags enabled for small pilot customers.
2) Week 1-4: Gradual enablement for Hosted tenants; onboard 5 early Dedicated Standard customers as pilot.
3) Week 5-8: Open Dedicated Pro sign-ups; beta rollout with selected enterprise customers.
4) Post GA (30-90 days): measure cost and latency impact; iterate on adaptive_window parameters.

Operational runbook highlights (summary):
- Key dashboards: Rollouts Overview, Route Health, Cost Insights per 1k tokens, Model Variant Capacity.
- Escalation path: if canary error_rate > 2% or p95 increases > 40% relative to baseline, Rollout Manager auto-pauses and notifies oncall-eng and product-sre.
- Rollback procedure (abridged):
  1. Pause rollout via Console or API.
  2. Evaluate logs and failure reason from fallback logs and tracing.
  3. If safe, rollback to previous variant and open postmortem; if not, escalate to Runtime team for hotfix.

Ownership and contacts:
- Product owner: Aisha Patel (product) — primary contact for roadmap and trade-offs.
- Engineering owners: Runtime Optimizer (owner: Marco Reyes, eng-serving-runtime); Routing & Rollouts (owner: Keiko Tanaka, eng-platform).
- SRE oncall: see eng-sre runbook for oncall roster.

Appendices:
- Appendix A: Benchmark summary (selected results):
  - Internal web-qa trace set: average token cost reduction 12.3%, p95 token latency reduction 16.1% on Dedicated Pro hardware profile.
- Appendix B: Example rollout policy templates (Console presets): balanced-default, latency-strict, cost-strict.

Notes and next steps:
- Action items for product & engineering before GA:
  - Finalize Dedicated SKUs (pricing/legal) and update pricing page (owner: finance).
  - Complete Console beta fixes for rollout controls (owner: eng-developer-experience).
  - Run controlled pilots with 3 anchor customers and collect telemetry for 30 days (owner: customer-success).

For detailed implementation tasks, ADRs, and engineering tickets, see related pages and the Roadmap epic in JIRA (linked in related_pages).
